CROP LOSS IN ODISHA 
 
810. MS. CHANDRANI MURMU: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृषि एवं कक सान क ल्याण मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that agriculture suffers in a big way due to both drought 
and cyclone in Odisha;  
(b) if so, whether any plan has been designed to compensate and support the farmers after 
such devastation;  
(c) the steps been taken in the last five years to support and compensate the farmers of 
Keonjhar district in Odisha; and  
(d) the estimated loss suffered by farmers due to mining activities in Keonjhar, if so, the steps 
that have been taken by the Government to compensate the loss? 
 
ANSWER 
 
 
MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
क ृषि एवं कक सान क ल्याण मंत्री (SHRI NARENDRA SINGH TOMAR) 
  
(a) to (c ): The State Government is primarily responsible for providing necessary relief 
measures in the wake of natural calamities. For undertaking relief measures, funds are 
available with the State Government in the form of the State Disaster Response Fund 
(SDRF). Additional financial assistance, over and above SDRF, is considered from the 
National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) for natural calamities of a severe nature and is 
approved on the basis of a Memorandum received from the State Government, in 
accordance with established procedures, which includes an assessment based on the visit of 
an Inter-Ministerial Central Team (IMCT). The financial assistance includes agriculture input 
subsidy as one of the components, which is computed for the affected area having crop  loss 
of 33% & above.

2022-23 are as under:

In addition, the Government of India has introduced yield based Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima 
Yojana (PMFBY) and weather based Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme 
(WBCIS) from Kharif 2016 to provide financial support to farmers suffering crop loss /damage 
arising out of natural calamities, adverse weather incidence and to stabilize income of 
farmers. Comprehensive risk insurance is provided under the scheme from pre -harvesting to 
post-harvest losses. Under this Scheme, claims are paid to only those farmers who have 
insured their crops and paid their share of premium under any of the notified crop insurance 
scheme in the notified area/crop by the State Government. The State Government of Odisha 
is implementing the scheme since its inception. 
  
(d):  Ministry of Mines has informed that data relating to loss suffered by farmers due to 
mining activities is not maintained in the Ministry. However, it has been reported that  land 
measuring 14687.02 hectares (10889.17 hectares - forest land & 3797.85 hectare s - other 
land) has been leased for mining purpose in Keonjhar district of Odisha.

Accountability of National Sporting Federations  
 
813. SHRI ANUBHAV MOHANTY:  
 
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) whether the Government plans to introduce a strong Sports Law 
that will govern every National Sporting Federations in the country 
considering the recent ban on All India Football Federation by FIFA, 
followed by warning to Indian Olympic Association by the 
International Olympic Committee;  
 
(b) if so, the details thereof;  
 
(c) whether the Government has any proposal to establish an 
autonomous body that will supervise various aspects of sports 
associations including elections, administrative functions an d 
dispute mechanism;  
 
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor;  
 
(e) the details of any other steps taken by the Government to 
ensure accountability of National Sporting Federations in the 
country; and  
 
(f) the details of grants g iven to various National Sporting 
Federations? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS 
(SHRI ANURAG SINGH THAKUR) 
 
(a) to (e): No, Sir. Governance and management of National Sports 
Federations (NSFs) is, at present, regulated in terms of the National 

Sports Development Code of India 2011 ( ‘’The Sports Code’’), which 
is an amalgamation of instructions and guidelines brought out by 
the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports. Provisions of the Sports Code 
are legally binding, as upheld by the Courts of Law.   
 
Under the Sports Code, t he Ministry ensures that  recognised NSFs 
abide by the basic and cardinal principles, such as  age &  tenure 
restrictions in respect of office bearers of the NSFs, conduct off air 
and transparent elections, protection of athletes’ interests, etc. The 
Government insists on observance of the provisions of the Sports 
Code by the NSFs to maintain their recognit ion on an year-to-year 
basis. Wherever any such violations are noticed, necessary action 
including suspension and withdrawal of recognition is taken.  
 
(f) The details of grants g iven to the various NSFs during the last 
three financial years are at Annexure.

SHRI VINAYAK RAUT: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the number of Gram Panchayats (GPs)  adopted under Sansad Adarsh Gram Yojana 
(SAGY), State and district-wise particularly in Maharashtra; 
(b)  the total amount of funds utilised under MPLADS, CSR under this yojana during each 
of the  last three years, State/UT and district -wise particularly  in the State of 
Maharashtra; 
(c)  the details of employment opportunities created  for skill development of people in 
villages under SAGY, State/UT and district-wise particularly of Maharashtra; and 
(d)  the details of schemes implemented for skill development and employment generation 
in the villages under SAGY, State/UT and district-wise particularly of Maharashtra? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a) The State and district -wise details of number of Gram Panchayats (GPs) adopted under 
Sansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (SAGY), including in the State of Maharashtra, are enclosed in 
Annexure-I. 
(b) As the development projects under Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana are implemented 
through mobilization of resources available under various Central and State Schemes, 
including MPLADS, CSR in convergence mode, the scheme specific data of funds utilised 
for development of villages is not maintained.  
  
(c) & (d):  The programmes like   Mahatma Gandhi National Employment Guarantee 
Scheme,  National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM) and Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen 
Kaushalya Yojana (DDU -GKY) of the Department of Rur al Development and Pradhan 
Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) of Ministry of Skill Development are being 
implemented for employment and skilling of rural youth and poor people across the country 
including in SAGY Gram Panchayats.   The PMKVY provides skill ing to 1 crore prospective 
youth under Short Term Training courses and Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) across the 
country including youth from SAGY Gram Panchayats. The Rural Self Employment Training 
Institutes (RSETIs) enable trainees to take Bank Cre dit for starting Micro -enterprises.  
Further, the Ministry has issued instructions to all State Rural Livelihood Missions (SRLMs) 
and Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs) on January 2015 to give priority in mobilization 
of candidates from Gram Panchayats i dentified under SAGY in the districts allotted in the 
sanctioned projects.  However, as all the SAGY projects are completed with the convergence 
of different schemes, the scheme specific data is not maintained.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COOPERATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 815 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 07/02/2023 
 
Digital Databse of Cooperative Societies 
 
815. SHRI G.M. SIDDESHWAR: 
 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकाįरता मंũी) be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government proposes to collect digital database of cooperative societies, 
including Primary Agricultural Credit Societies and Multi-State cooperatives all over the 
country and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) the time by which the database will be ready for use by various stakeholders; 
 
(c) whether any committee or inquiry has been constituted to go into the irregularities and 
embezzlement of funds which occurred in the various cooperatives in the country and if so, 
the details thereof; and 
 
(d) if not, the measures taken by the Government to deal with such irregularities and to bring 
the cooperatives to normal health? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकाįरता मंũी (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a) & (b): Yes Sir. Ministry of Cooperation has initiated the process of developing an 
exhaustive digital database of cooperative societies namely National Cooperative Database 
for having an authentic & updated data repository of cooperatives working in all sectors 
including Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) and Multi-State cooperatives all over 
the country.The proposed Database will facilitate all stakeholders in policy making & 
implementation to strengthen the cooperative movement in the country. For Phase-I of 
National Cooperative Database, data collection of three cooperative sectors i.e. PACS, Dairy 
and Fisheries has been started from 1stDecember, 2022 and would be available for use by 
various stakeholders by the end of February, 2023. 
(c): As per statutory provisions, action is to be taken by Central Registrar of Cooperative 
Societies (CRCS) in case of Muti-State Cooperative Societies registered under Muti-State 
Cooperative Societies Act, 2002 and State Registrar of Cooperative Society (RCS) in case of 
Societies registered under the respective State Cooperative Acts, whenever any complaint of 
irregularities is received. 
(d): In order to realize the vision of “Sahakar-se-Samriddhi”, promote cooperative based 
economic development model, strengthen cooperative movement and deepen its reach up to 

the grassroots, Ministry of Cooperation since its formation in July, 2021 has taken various 
initiatives such as: 
 
1. Computerization of PACS: Process to onboard 63,000 functional PACS on an ERP based 
common national software with an outlay of ₹2,516 Crore started.  
 
2. Model byelaws for PACS: Model byelaws prepared and circulated for their adoption as 
per the respective State Cooperatives Act to enable PACS to undertake more than 25 
business activities like dairy, fishery, setting up of godowns, LPG/ Petrol/ Green energy 
distribution agency, banking correspondents, CSC, etc. 
 
3. PACS as Common Service Centres (CSC): MoU signed between Ministry of 
Cooperation, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, NABARD and CSC -
SPV to facilitate functioning of PACS as CSCs to improve their viability, provide e-
services at village level and generate employment. 
 
4. National Cooperative Database: Preparation of an authentic and updated data repository 
of cooperatives in the country started to facilitate stakeholders in policy making and 
implementation.  
 
5. National Cooperative Policy: A National level committee comprising of experts and 
stakeholders drawn from all over the Country constituted to formulate the New 
Cooperation Policy to create an enabling ecosystem to realize the vision of ‘Sahakar-se-
Samriddhi’. 
 
6. Amendment of MSCS Act, 2002: Bill introduced in the Parliament to amend the centrally 
administered MSCS Act, 2002 to incorporate provisions of 97th Constitutional 
Amendment, strengthen governance, enhance transparency, increase accountability and 
reform electoral process in the Multi State Cooperative Societies. 
 
7. National Cooperative Development Corporation: New schemes for cooperatives launched 
by NCDC in various sectors such as ‘Swayamshakti Sahkar’ for SHG; ‘Deerghavadhi 
Krishak Sahkar’ for long term agricultural credit; ‘Dairy Sahkar’ for dairy and ‘Neel 
Sahkar’ for fisheries. Total financial assistance of Rs. 34,221 Crores disbursed in FY 
2021-22. 
  
8. Member Lending Institutions in Credit Guarantee Fund Trust: Non-scheduled UCBs, 
StCBs and DCCBs notified as MLIs in CGTMSE Scheme to increase share of 
cooperatives in lending. 
 
9. Cooperatives as ‘buyers’ on GeM portal:  Cooperatives permitted to register as ‘buyer’ 
on GeM, enabling them to procure goods and services from nearly 40 lakh vendors to 
facilitate economical purchases and greater transparency. 
 

10. Reduction in surcharge on cooperative societies: Surcharge reduced from 12 % to 7% for 
cooperative societies having income between Rs. 1 to 10 Cr.  
 
11. Reduction in Minimum Alternate Tax: MAT reduced for cooperatives from 18.5% to 
15%. 
 
12. Relief under Section 269ST of IT Act: A clarification has been issued to remove 
difficulties in cash transactions by cooperatives under Section 269ST of IT Act. 
 
13. Lowering tax rate for new cooperatives: Announcement made in the Union Budget 2023-
24 to charge flat lower tax rate of 15%, compared with current rate of upto 30% plus 
surcharge, for new cooperatives commencing manufacturing activities till March 31, 
2024.  
 
14. Increase in limit of deposits and loans in cash by PACS and PCARDBs:  Announcement 
made in the Union Budget 2023-24 to increase limit from Rs. 20,000 to Rs. 2 lakh per 
member for deposits and loans in cash by PACS and PCARDBs. 
 
15. Increase in limit for TDS: Announcement made in the Union Budget 2023-24 to increase 
cash withdrawal limit for cooperatives from Rs. 1 Crore to Rs. 3 Crore, per annum, 
without being subjected to TDS.  
 
16. Relief to Sugar Cooperative Mills: Sugar cooperative mills not to be subjected to 
additional income tax for paying higher sugarcane prices to farmers upto Fair and 
Remunerative or State Advised Price. 
 
17. Resolution of chronic pending issues of Sugar Cooperative Mills: Announcement made 
in the Union Budget 2023-24 to allow sugar cooperatives to claim as expenditure their 
payments to sugarcane farmers for the period prior to assessment year 2016–17, giving a 
relief of nearly Rs. 10,000 crores. 
  
18. New National Multi-State Cooperative Seed Society: New apex national multi-state 
cooperative seed society being established under the MSCS Act, 2002 as umbrella 
organization for quality seed cultivation, production and distribution under a single 
brand. 
 
19. New National Multi-State Cooperative Organic Society: New apex national multi-state 
cooperative organic society being established under the MSCS Act, 2002 as umbrella 
organization to produce, distribute and market certified and authentic organic products. 
 
20. New National Multi-State Cooperative Export Society: New apex national multi-state 
cooperative export society being established under the MSCS Act, 2002 as umbrella 
organization togive thrust to exports from cooperative sector.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 816 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 07TH FEBRUARY, 2023/ MAGHA 18, 1944 (SAKA) 
 
CYBER CRIMES  
 
†816.  SHRI BASANTA KUMAR PANDA:  
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether there is any organised department to deal with the cyber 
crimes and if so, the details and the nature of online transaction thereof;  
 
(b) the steps taken by the Government to prevent OTP based and other 
cyber frauds;  
 
c) the number of cyber frauds registered on the central helpline of the 
Government from other States including Odisha and the extent to which 
successful efforts were made to prevent them and action taken in this 
regard along with the number of cases disposed of; 
 
(d) whether the Government has provided additional funds to the States for 
better equipment of their cyber police stations; and 
 
(e) if so, the details thereof, State/UT-wise including Odisha?  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI AJAY KUMAR MISHRA) 
(a) & (b):  ‘Police’ and ‘Public Order’ are State subjects as per the Seventh 
Schedule of the Constitution of India. The States/UTs are primarily 
responsible for the prevention, detection, investigation and prosecution of 
crimes  including  cyber  crimes  through  their Law Enforcement Agencies  

--2-- 
L.S. US.Q. NO. 816 FOR 07.02.2023 
(LEAs). The LEAs take legal action as per the provisions of law against 
persons involved in cyber crime. The Central Government supplements the 
initiatives of the States/UTs through advisories and financial assistance 
under various schemes for their capacity building. 
To strengthen the mechanism to deal with cyber crimes in a 
comprehensive and coordinated manner, the Central Government has 
taken steps which, inter-alia, include the following: 
(i) Ministry of Home Affairs has set up the ‘Indian Cyber Crime 
Coordination Centre (I4C)’ to deal with all types of cyber crime in the 
country, in a coordinated and comprehensive manner.    
(ii) The National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (www.cybercrime.gov.in) 
has been launched on 30th August 2019, as a part of the I4C, to enable 
public to report incidents pertaining to all types of cyber crimes, with 
special focus on cyber crimes against women and children. Cyber crime 
incidents reported on this portal, their conversion into FIRs and 
subsequent action thereon are handled by the State/UT Law Enforcement 
Agencies (LEAs) concerned as per the provisions of the law.  
(iii) The Citizen  Financial  Cyber Fraud Reporting and  Management 
System, under I4C, has been launched for immediate reporting of financial 
frauds   and   to  stop  siphoning   off  funds  by  the  fraudsters.  A  toll-free  

--3-- 
L.S. US.Q. NO. 816 FOR 07.02.2023 
Helpline number ‘1930’ has been operationalized to get assistance in 
lodging online cyber complaints. 
(iv) The Massive Open Online Courses (MOOC) platform, namely ‘CyTrain’ 
portal has been developed under the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination 
Centre (I4C), for capacity building of police officers/judicial officers 
through online course on critical aspects of cyber crime investigation, 
forensics, prosecution etc. along with certification. More than 28,700 
Police Officers from States/UTs are registered and more than 7,800 
Certificates issued through the portal. 
(v) Seven Joint Cyber Coordination Teams have been constituted under 
I4C by on boarding States/UTs to address the challenges of cyber crime 
hotspots/areas having multi jurisdictional issues to enhance the 
coordination framework among the LEAs of the States/UTs. 
(vi) To spread awareness on cyber crime, the Central Government has  
taken  steps  which,  inter-alia,  include;  dissemination   of messages 
through SMS, I4C social media account i.e. Twitter handle (@CyberDost), 
Facebook (CyberDostI4C), Instagram (CyberDostI4C), Telegram 
(cyberdosti4C), Radio campaign, etc., engaged MyGov for publicity in 
multiple     mediums,   organizing  Cyber  Safety  and  Security   Awareness 
 

--4-- 
L.S. US.Q. NO. 816 FOR 07.02.2023 
weeks in association with States/UTs, publishing of Handbook for 
Adolescents/Students, etc. The States/UTs have also been requested to 
carry out publicity to create mass awareness. 
 (c): Since inception of Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and 
Management System, more than 7 lakh complaints have been registered 
including in Odisha till January 31, 2023. So far, financial amount of more 
than Rs. 235 Crore have been saved in more than 1.90 lakh complaints. 
More than 52,000 complaints have been disposed of. 
(d) & (e): Ministry of Home Affairs has provided central assistance under 
‘Assistance to States for Modernization of Police’ Scheme to the State 
Governments for the acquisition of latest weaponry, training gadgets, 
advanced communication/forensic equipment, Cyber Policing equipment 
etc. The State Governments formulate State Action Plans (SAPs) as per 
their strategic priorities and requirements including combating cyber 
crimes. State/UT- wise details of the amounts of Central financial 
assistance disbursed under this scheme during the last 4 financial years is 
placed at Annexure-I.

Training Centres of SAI 
 
817. DR. KALANIDHI VEERASWAMY: 
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) the number of Sports Authority of India (SAI) Training Centres in the 
country including Tamil Nadu; 
(b) the details of the training being provided at these centres; 
(c) the details of the funds sanctioned, allocated and utilized by these 
centres including in Tamil Nadu during the last three years and the 
current year; 
(d) the details of the targets set and achievements made so far; 
(e) whether the Government is aware that there is also a requirement 
of SAI Training Centre in North Chennai and if so, the details thereof; 
(f) whether the Government is proposing to establish such centre in 
North Chennai; and 
(g) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS 
[SHRI ANURAG SINGH THAKUR]  
 
(a) and (b): There are 69 Sports Authority of India (SAI) Training Centres 
(STCs) in the country out of which 4 Centres are located in Tamil Nadu.  
The details of discipline-wise training provided at these Centres are at 
Annexure-I. 
 

The athletes for training at the STCs are provided support in the form 
of expert coaches, sports equipment, boarding and lodging, sports kit, 
competition exposure, educational expenses, medical/ insurance and 
stipend as per the approved scheme norms. 
 
(c):  SAI releases funds to its Regional Centres on a regular basis. The 
details of the funds allocated to SAI Regional Centres and utilization 
for the last three years and current year under Block Grant SAI are 
attached at Annexure-II. LNCPE Trivandrum is located in Tamil Nadu 
and the details of the funds released for centres in Tamil Nadu are 
mentioned against RC LNCPE Trivandrum. 
(d):  Sports being a dynamic and progressive activity, setting of 
targets is not feasible. The details of the achievements of athletes of 
SAI Sports Promotional Schemes are attached at Annexure-III.  
(e) to (g):  No proposal has been received from the State Government 
of Tamil Nadu so far. SAI has undertaken an exercise of restructuring 
of its Sports Promotional Schemes taking into account the available 
infrastructure at the training centres as well as the prevailing financial 
constraints. Therefore, it has been decided to focus on the existing 
centres.

DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES

UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 818 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 07TH FEBRUARY, 2023 
Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairy Projects 
818.DR. AMOL RAMSING KOLHE:  
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING, मत्स्यपालन 
पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री be pleased to state: 
(a) Whether the Government has received any proposal from the State of Maharashtra regarding 
setting up of fisheries, animal husbandry and dairy projects under the centrally sponsored schemes 
and if so, the details thereof and the response of the Government thereto;  
(b) the details of various schemes being implemented by the Government for the development of 
Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairy sector in the State of Maharashtra during the last three 
years;  
(c) the total number of farmers who have been benefited by these schemes so far;  
(d) whether the Government has failed to achieve the growth rate targets in the said sector and if 
so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor; and  
(e) the details of corrective steps taken by the Government to promote the ani mal husbandry and 
fisheries sectors in the country? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA) 
(a) to (e): The Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairyi ng, Government of India is  
implementing the following schemes and programme in the country including the State of 
Maharashtra for all round development of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairy Sectors:  
1. Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY),  
2. Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF),  
3. Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM),  
4. National Livestock Mission (NLM),  
5. National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD),  
6. Dairy Processing and Infrastructure Development Fund (DIDF),  
7. Supporting Dairy Cooperatives and Farmer Producer Organizations (SDCFPO)  
8. Entrepreneurship Development and Employment Generation (EDEG), and  
9. Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme (LHDCP). 
  

In respect of Fisheries Sector, under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana, the Department 
of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying during the financial years, 
2020-21, 2021-22 and 2022-23 has approved the proposals of Government of Maharashtra to the 
tune of Rs. 792.32 crore with total central share of Rs. 355.32 crore for development of fisheries 
and aquaculture sector in the state  benefitting an estimated 13603 beneficiaries including fish 
farmers. Further, under Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund, t he 
Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries , Animal Husbandry and Dairying  so far has 
accorded approval to the project proposals with a total outlay of Rs. 943.69 crore to  the State of 
Maharashtra including the proposals of private beneficiaries for providing concessional finance in 
the form of interest subvention of up to 3%.  
In respect of Dairy Sector, u nder the National Programme for Dairy Development ( NPDD) 
scheme, three projects have been approved for Maharashtra with a total outlay of Rs. 49 .47 crore 
and central share being Rs. 45.07 crore. An amount of Rs. 31.92 crore has been released till date . 
Under Dairy Processing and Infrastructure Development Fund  (DIDF), 2 projects have been 
sanctioned for the state of Maharashtra  at a total cost of Rs. 488.33 crore and loan amount of Rs 
290.66 crore for providing interest subvention. Under DIDF, 1.9 lakh farmers have been indirectly 
benefitted in Maharashtra as on 31-12-2022. Further, under the central sector scheme Supporting 
Dairy Cooperatives and Farmer Producer Orga nizations engaged in dairy activities  (SDCFPO), 
the National Dairy Development Board  (NDDB) has released an interest subvention of Rs . 4.40 
crore for the year 2020 -21 and Rs . 4.71 crore for the year 2021 -22 for two milk unions  in 
Maharashtra State.   
In respect of Animal Husbandry Sector, under Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development 
Fund (AHIDF), 36 projects have been sanctioned for the state of Maharashtra at a total cost of Rs 
1325.61 crore and loan amount of Rs. 947.72 crore for providing interest subvention. Further, the 
State Government has also submitted a proposal for Livestock Insurance and the same has been 
approved. Under Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM), an amount of Rs 68.96 crore has been released 
to Maharashtra.  Under Livestock Health and D isease Control Programme (LHDCP) , i n 
Maharashtra 1,47,11,259 animals have been vaccinated for Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) during 
Round-I, 1,68,78,945 animals have been vaccinated for FMD during Round-II, 3,74,523 animals 
have been vaccinated for Brucella and 43,263 animals have been vaccinated for Peste des Petits 
Ruminants (PPR). Support has been extended to Maharashtra state for establishing and 
strengthening mobile veterinary units (MVUs) and 80 such MVUs have been sanctioned and funds 
to the tune of Rs.12.90 crore have been released. Under the Nationwide Artificial Insemination 
Program of Rashtriya Gokul Mission, 20.69 lakh farmers of Maharashtra have been benefitted.   
The Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairy Sectors are showing buoyant growth in recent years. 
The fish production of Maharashtra has increased from 5.23 lakh tons in 2020-21 to 5.89 lakh tons 
during 2021-22 recording 12.6% increase in comparison to the year 2020-21. The growth target of 
Animal Husbandry sector of Mahara shtra has been promising from 3.8% in 20 12-13 to 11% in 
2020-21.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COOPERATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 819 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 07/02/2023 
 
National Policy on Cooperation 
 
819.    SHRI ACHYUTANANDA SAMANTA: 
 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकाįरता मंũी) be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has proposed to introduce National Policy on Cooperation and if so, the 
details thereof; and  
(b) the steps taken by the Government for strengthening India’s cooperative architecture syncing it 
with country’s economic and social needs? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकाįरता मंũी (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a): Yes, Sir. A National level committee has been constituted on 2nd September 2022 under the 
chairmanship of Shri Suresh Prabhakar Prabhu, consisting of experts of the cooperative sector, 
representatives from National/ State/ District/ Primary level cooperative societies, Secretaries 
(Cooperation) and RCSs from States/UTs, officers from Central Ministries/ Departments to formulate 
the New National Cooperation Policy. The formulation of New National Cooperation Policy will help 
in realising the vision of 'Sahakar se Samriddhi', promoting the cooperative based economic 
development model, strengthening the cooperative movement in the country and deepening its reach 
up to the grassroots. In this regard, consultations were earlier held with stakeholders and suggestions 
for formulating the new Policy were invited from the Central Ministries/ Departments, States/UTs, 
National Cooperative Federations, Institutions and also from the general public. The National level 
committee will analyse the collated feedback, policy suggestions & recommendations to formulate the 
draft of the new Policy. 
 
(b): Number of steps have been taken by the Government, after the formation of the Ministry of 
Cooperation, to strengthen India’s cooperative architecture syncing it with country’s economic and 
social needs, inter-alia, including the following:  
1. Computerization of PACS: Process to onboard 63,000 functional PACS on an ERP based common 
national software with an outlay of ₹2,516 Crore started.  
 

2. Model byelaws for PACS: Model byelaws prepared and circulated for their adoption as per the 
respective State Cooperatives Act to enable PACS to undertake more than 25 business activities 
like dairy, fishery, setting up of godowns, LPG/ Petrol/ Green energy distribution agency, banking 
correspondents, CSC, etc. 
 
3. PACS as Common Service Centres (CSC): MoU signed between Ministry of Cooperation, Ministry 
of Electronics and Information Technology, NABARD and CSC -SPV to facilitate functioning of 
PACS as CSCs to improve their viability, provide e-services at village level and generate 
employment. 
 
4. National Cooperative Database: Preparation of an authentic and updated data repository of 
cooperatives in the country started to facilitate stakeholders in policy making and implementation.  
 
5. National Cooperative Policy: A National level committee comprising of experts and stakeholders 
drawn from all over the Country constituted to formulate the New Cooperation Policy to create an 
enabling ecosystem to realize the vision of ‘Sahakar-se-Samriddhi’. 
 
6. Amendment of MSCS Act, 2002: Bill introduced in the Parliament to amend the centrally 
administered MSCS Act, 2002 to incorporate provisions of 97th Constitutional Amendment, 
strengthen governance, enhance transparency, increase accountability and reform electoral process 
in the Multi State Cooperative Societies. 
 
7. National Cooperative Development Corporation: New schemes for cooperatives launched by 
NCDC in various sectors such as ‘Swayamshakti Sahkar’ for SHG; ‘Deerghavadhi Krishak Sahkar’ 
for long term agricultural credit; ‘Dairy Sahkar’ for dairy and ‘Neel Sahkar’ for fisheries. Total 
financial assistance of Rs. 34,221 Crores disbursed in FY 2021-22. 
 
8. Member Lending Institutions in Credit Guarantee Fund Trust: Non-scheduled UCBs, StCBs and 
DCCBs notified as MLIs in CGTMSE Scheme to increase share of cooperatives in lending. 
 
9. Cooperatives as ‘buyers’ on GeM portal:  Cooperatives permitted to register as ‘buyer’ on GeM, 
enabling them to procure goods and services from nearly 40 lakh vendors  to facilitate economical 
purchases and greater transparency. 
 
10. Reduction in surcharge on cooperative societies: Surcharge reduced from 12 % to 7% for co-
operative societies having income between Rs. 1 to 10 Cr.  
 
11. Reduction in Minimum Alternate Tax: MAT reduced for Co-operatives from 18.5% to 15%. 
 
12. Relief under Section 269ST of IT Act: A clarification has been issued to remove difficulties in each 
transaction by cooperatives under Section 269ST of IT Act. 
 

13. Lowering tax rate for new cooperatives: Announcement made in the Union Budget 2023-24 to 
charge flat lower tax rate of 15%, compared with current rate of upto 30% plus surcharge, for new 
cooperatives commencing manufacturing activities till March 31, 2024.  
 
14. Increase in limit of deposits and loans in cash by PACS and PCARDBs:  Announcement made in 
the Union Budget 2023-24 to increase limit from Rs. 20,000 to Rs. 2 lakh per member for deposits 
and loans in cash by PACS and PCARDBs. 
 
15. Increase in limit for TDS: Announcement made in the Union Budget 2023-24 to increase cash 
withdrawal limit for cooperatives from Rs. 1 Crore to Rs. 3 Crore, per annum, without being 
subjected to TDS.  
 
16. Relief to Sugar Cooperative Mills: Sugar co-operative mills not to be subjected to additional 
income tax for paying higher sugarcane prices to farmers upto Fair and Remunerative or State 
Advised Price. 
 
17. Resolution of chronic pending issues of Sugar Cooperative Mills: Announcement made in the 
Union Budget 2023-24 to allow sugar cooperatives to claim as expenditure their payments to 
sugarcane farmers for the period prior to assessment year 2016–17, giving a relief of nearly Rs. 
10,000 crores. 
 
18. New National Multi-State Cooperative Seed Society: New apex national multi-state cooperative 
seed society being established under the MSCS Act, 2002 as umbrella organization for quality seed 
cultivation, production and distribution under a single brand. 
 
19. New National Multi-State Cooperative Organic Society: New apex national multi-state cooperative 
organic society being established under the MSCS Act, 2002 as umbrella organization to produce, 
distribute and market certified and authentic organic products. 
 
20. New National Multi-State Cooperative Export Society: New apex national multi-state cooperative 
export society being established under the MSCS Act, 2002 as umbrella organization to give thrust 
to exports from cooperative sector.

NATURAL FARMING IN RAINFED AREAS 
 
 
821. SHRI SANJAY BHATIA: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ षि एवं ककसान  कल्याण मंत्री  
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is focusing on the promotion of natural farming in rainfed 
areas beyond Ganga as well as Yamuna river and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) whether the Union Government has any p roposal to bring any new plans/economic 
plans and development projects in coordination with the State Government in those districts 
of Haryana (Karnal, Panipat, Kurukshetra etc.) which produce for agriculture market and 
export at international level; and 
 
(c) if so, the details thereof?

क ृ षि एवं ककसान  कल्याण मंत्री     (SHRI NARENDRA SINGH TOMAR) 
 
(a): Government is promoting natural farming through a sub scheme namely Bhartiya

  822. SHRI RAMESH CHANDRA MAJHI: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृषि एवं कक सान क ल्याण मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has received any complaints/suggestion on the coverage of 
crops under Minimum Support Price (MSP) scheme and if so, the details thereof;  
(b) the percentage of MSP coverage for all crops during the last five years;  
(c) whether it is true that there are crops covered under MSP but not procured from farmers 
at that price and if so, the reasons therefor, crop-wise;  
(d) whether the Government is taking steps to increase the coverage  of MSP on all crops 
and if so, the details thereof; and  
(e) if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
क ृषि एवं कक सान क ल्याण मंत्री      (SHRI NARENDRA SINGH TOMAR) 
 
(a) to (e): Government fixes Minimum Support Prices (MSP) for 22 mandated agricultural 
crops and Fair & Remunerative Price (FRP) for sugarcane on the basis of the 
recommendations of the Commiss ion for Agricultural Costs & Prices (CACP), after 
considering the views of State Governments and Central Ministries/Departments concerned 
and other relevant factors.CACP also holdsconsultations withall the stakeholders and seeks 
suggestions for both price and non -price recommendations. Suggestions/Representations 

 
 
 
from State Governments and various farmer organizations are also received from time to 
time for the coverage of crops under MSP . The inclusion of crops under MSP framework is  
however, dependent on several factors which include essential for food security , relatively 
large shelf life, widely grown, item of mass consumption, among others.  
To realize the objective MSP Policy, Government extends price support for paddy and 
wheat through the Food Corpor ation of India (FCI) and State Agencies. Under this policy, 
whatever food grains are offered by farmers within the stipulated period & conforming to the 
specifications prescribed by Government are purchased at MSP by the State Government 
agencies including  FCI for Central Pool. Additionally, Oilseeds, pulses and copra of Fair 
Average Quality (FAQ) are procured from registered farmers under Price Support Scheme 
under Umbrella Scheme of PM-AASHA, as per its guidelines at MSP in consultation with the 
concerned State Government as and when market price of these produce fall below the 
MSP. Details of crop-wise procurement at MSP for last five years is given at annexure.

SMALL FOOD PROCESSING COLD CHAIN  
  
824. SHRI KULDEEP RAI SHARMA: 
  
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
  
(a)  the number of small food processing cold chain set up/functioning in the country; 
(b)  whether the Government has any proposal to provide grants for establishing small food 
processing cold chain units in near future; 
(c)  if so, the details thereof, especially in Andaman & Nicobar Islands and if not, the reasons

processing units and if so, the details thereof?  
 
  
ANSWER

(SHRI PRAHLAD SINGH PATEL)

proposals are invited from interested individuals/ entities through Expression of Interest (EoI) floated 
from time to time and projects are sanctioned based on procedure enumerated in the scheme guidelines.

Islands, out of which one is completed.  
(d):  Interested individuals can avai l benefits available under Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro

DOMINO EFFECT IN MGNREGS 
 
826.  SHRI MANICKAM TAGORE B.: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether it is a fact that the Government owes as on December 14, 2022, Rs. 4,700 
crore in wages to 18 States and Rs. 5,450 crore in material cost to 19 States and if so, 
the details thereof; 
(b)  whether it is also a fact that the delay in material costs has a domino effect on work 
since a delay in the payment breaks the supply chain and if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether it is also true that the vendors are reluctant to supply new material because of 
prolonged delays in payments and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d)  whether it is also true that the Government is considering meeting the shortfall and if 
so, the details and the manner thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
 
(a),(b)&(d): Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (Mahatma 
Gandhi NREGS) is a demand driven wage employment Scheme. Funds are released to the 
States/UTs on the basis of "agreed to" Labour Budget (LB) and performance of the 
States/UTs during the financial year. Fund release to States/UTs is a continuous process and 
Central Government is committed to making funds available keeping in view the demand for 
work on the ground. No State/UT -wise financial allocation is made under Mahatma Gandhi 
NREGS.  
  
During the current financial year 2022 -23 (as on 03.02.2023) an amount of Rs. 72813.73 
crore was released for wage, material & administrative components under Mahatma Gandhi 
NREGS.

Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether it is true that the Government proposes to develop rural areas by provisioning 
of economic, social and physical infrastructure facilities under the Shyama Prasad 
Mukherji Rurban Mission (SPMRM); 
(b)  if so, whether it is also true that the mission aims to develop 300 Rurban clusters 
within the year 2025; and 
(c)  the detail of clusters which have been taken up in West Bengal and the funds 
disbursed for the same and if no cluster has been taken up, the reasons therefor?

(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a)& (b)   Shyama Prasad Mukherji  Rurban Mission (SPMRM) was launched on 
21st February 2016 by the Government of India to develop 300 Rurban clusters across India 
as socially, economically and physically sustainable regions by providing economic, social 
and infrastructure amenities. The Mission was launched initially for a period u p to March, 
2020. Thereafter, “sunset date” for the scheme was declared as 31st March 2022.  
  
(c) The State of West Bengal was allocated 14 clusters, out of which, the State identified 
only 10 clusters. The details of the clusters identified is at Annexur e 1. However, out of 14 
clusters allocated, 7 clusters were withdrawn by the Government of India from the State of 
West Bengal in January 2021, as no progress was made in these clusters.  
 
The Integrated Cluster Action Plan (ICAP) for the remaining 7 clust ers allocated was 
approved by the Ministry in March 2016. Rs. 35.10 crore was released as Central share of 
Critical Gap Fund (CGF) and Rs. 1.05 crore was released as administrative fund to the State. 
However, no further progress was made by the State in th e implementation of Mission. The 
State returned the CGF amount to the Consolidated Fund of India.

†832. SHRI DHARAMBIR SINGH:  
 
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of Gram Panchayats where financial irregularities have been found so far 
and the action taken against the said Gram Panchayats in the country, State -wise 
including Haryana;  
 
(b) whether the Government has conducted any enquiry in this regard; and  
 
(c) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI KAPIL MORESHWAR PATIL) 
 
(a) to (c) Panchayat, being “Local Government”, is a State subject in terms of the State list of 
Seventh Schedule of Constitution of India. Mandate for setting  up of Panchayats is provided 
by Article 243 in Part IX of the Constitution of India. The Panchayats are setup and operated 
through the respective State Panchayati Raj Acts. Accordingly, Panchayats are primarily the 
responsibility of concerned State Governments and appropriate actions on complaints relating 
to all issues of  Panchayats including financial irregularities is the responsibility of State 
Governments. Any references of complaints against Panchayats including financial 
irregularities received in t he Ministry are duly forwarded to the concern State Government 
for necessary action. Ministry does not maintain records of follow up action taken by the 
States on such complaints.

Establishing of Multi-State Co-operatives 
 
833: SHRI D.K. SURESH: 
SHRIMATI SUMALATHA AMBAREESH: 
 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकाįरता मंũी) be pleased to state: 
(a) the total number of Multi-State Co-operatives established in the country during the last three years, 
year wise and State-wise;  
(b) whether the Government has mandated the Co-operatives to help in ease of doing business in tune 
with the vision of promoting business opportunity in the country, if so, the details thereof; and  
(c) whether the Government has put any mechanism in place to monitor the functioning of the Multi-
State co-operatives and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION  
सहकाįरता मंũी (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a): The total number of multi-State cooperative societies established in the country during the last 
three years, year wise and State-wiseis attached at Annexure-I.  
 
(b): In order to realize the vision of “Sahakar-se-Samriddhi”, promote cooperative based economic 
development model, strengthen cooperative movement and deepen its reach up to the grassroots, 
Ministry of Cooperation since its formation in July, 2021 has taken various initiatives such as: 
1. Computerization of PACS: Process to onboard 63,000 functional PACS on an ERP based 
common national software with an outlay of ₹2,516 Crore started.  
 
2. Model byelaws for PACS: Model byelaws prepared and circulated for their adoption as per the 
respective State Cooperatives Act to enable PACS to undertake more than 25 business activities 
like dairy, fishery, setting up of godowns, LPG/ Petrol/ Green energy distribution agency, 
banking correspondents, CSC, etc. 
 
3. PACS as Common Service Centres (CSC): MoU signed between Ministry of Cooperation, 
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, NABARD and CSC -SPV to facilitate 
functioning of PACS as CSCs to improve their viability, provide e-services at village level and 
generate employment. 
 
 

4. National Cooperative Database: Preparation of an authentic and updated data repository of 
cooperatives in the country started to facilitate stakeholders in policy making and 
implementation.  
 
5. National Cooperative Policy: A National level committee comprising of experts and stakeholders 
drawn from all over the Country constituted to formulate the New Cooperation Policy to create 
an enabling ecosystem to realize the vision of ‘Sahakar-se-Samriddhi’. 
 
6. Amendment of MSCS Act, 2002: Bill introduced in the Parliament to amend the centrally 
administered MSCS Act, 2002 to incorporate provisions of 97th Constitutional Amendment, 
strengthen governance, enhance transparency, increase accountability and reform electoral 
process in the Multi State Cooperative Societies. 
 
7. National Cooperative Development Corporation: New schemes for cooperatives launched by 
NCDC in various sectors such as ‘Swayamshakti Sahkar’ for SHG; ‘Deerghavadhi Krishak 
Sahkar’ for long term agricultural credit; ‘Dairy Sahkar’ for dairy and ‘Neel Sahkar’ for 
fisheries. Total financial assistance of Rs. 34,221 Crores disbursed in FY 2021-22. 
 
8. Member Lending Institutions in Credit Guarantee Fund Trust: Non-scheduled UCBs, StCBs and 
DCCBs notified as MLIs in CGTMSE Scheme to increase share of cooperatives in lending. 
 
9. Cooperatives as ‘buyers’ on GeM portal:  Cooperatives permitted to register as ‘buyer’ on GeM, 
enabling them to procure goods and services from nearly 40 lakh vendors  to facilitate 
economical purchases and greater transparency. 
 
10. Reduction in surcharge on cooperative societies: Surcharge reduced from 12 % to 7% for co-
operative societies having income between Rs. 1 to 10 Cr.  
 
11. Reduction in Minimum Alternate Tax: MAT reduced for cooperatives from 18.5% to 15%. 
 
12. Relief under Section 269ST of IT Act: A clarification has been issued to remove difficulties in 
cash transactions by cooperatives under Section 269ST of IT Act. 
 
13. Lowering tax rate for new cooperatives: Announcement made in the Union Budget 2023-24 to 
charge flat lower tax rate of 15%, compared with current rate of upto 30% plus surcharge, for 
new cooperatives commencing manufacturing activities till March 31, 2024.  
 
14. Increase in limit of deposits and loans in cash by PACS and PCARDBs:  Announcement made in 
the Union Budget 2023-24 to increase limit from Rs. 20,000 to Rs. 2 lakh per member for 
deposits and loans in cash by PACS and PCARDBs. 
 
15. Increase in limit for TDS: Announcement made in the Union Budget 2023-24 to increase cash 
withdrawal limit for cooperatives from Rs. 1 Crore to Rs. 3 Crore, per annum, without being 
subjected to TDS.  
 

16. Relief to Sugar Cooperative Mills: Sugar cooperative mills not to be subjected to additional 
income tax for paying higher sugarcane prices to farmers upto Fair and Remunerative or State 
Advised Price. 
  
17. Resolution of chronic pending issues of Sugar Cooperative Mills: Announcement made in the 
Union Budget 2023-24 to allow sugar cooperatives to claim as expenditure their payments to 
sugarcane farmers for the period prior to assessment year 2016–17, giving a relief of nearly Rs. 
10,000 crores. 
 
18. New National Multi-State Cooperative Seed Society: New apex national multi-state cooperative 
seed society being established under the MSCS Act, 2002 as umbrella organization for quality

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 835 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 7TH  FEBRUARY, 2023 
 
Extinction of Ornamental Fishes  
 
835. SHRIMATI SARMISTHA SETHI: 
 
        Will the  Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING मत्स्यपालन, 
पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Ministry is aware of smuggling of rare fishes both in domestic market and to other 
countries; 
(b) If so, the details thereof and the steps taken by the Government to prevent this; 
(c) whether the Ministry is aware of extinction of several rare ornamental fishes in India; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof and the steps taken to ensure that the extinction does not take place? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING: 
(SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA) 
(a) and (b): The Government of India under Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change 
(MoEF&CC) has set up a  Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB) to gather intelligence about 
poaching and unlawful trade in wild animals and animal artic les and to achieve inter -state and 
transboundary coordination in enforcement of wildlife laws. A total of five incidents of shark fin 
smuggling from 2019 have been reported by WCCB  and action has been taken by the concerned 
authorities as per the provisions of Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 as well as the Custom Act, 1962  
read with FT (D&R) Act, 1992 . The Wildlife Crime Control Bureau issues regular alerts, advisories 
and also assists and advises Custom authorities in inspection of the consignments of flo ra & fauna as 
per the provisions of Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972, Convention on International Trade in 
Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) and EXIM Policy governing such items. 
(c) and (d): The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR)  and Zoological Survey of India 
(ZSI) have reported that there is no extinction of ornamental fish species in India. For conservation 
of declining indigenous ornamental fish stock, the research institutes under aegis of ICAR are 
organizing sensitization and awareness programme. Further, ICAR has launched All India Network 
Project on Ornamental Fish Culture for developing seed production and culture technologies of 
potential ornamental finfish/shellfish.

O.I.H. 
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
LOK  SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 836 
  ANSWERED ON 07/02/2023 
 
MONITORING OF NGOS 
 
836.  SHRI BALAK NATH: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether funds are being provided by the Union Government to Non-Governmental 
Organizations (NGOs) for implementing projects under rural development schemes in 
the country including Rajasthan and if so, the details thereof; 
(b)  whether the progress of work done by the said NGOs has been monitored by the 
Union Government; and 
(c)  if so, the details along with the outcome thereof ? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a) to (c) : The Department of Rural Development, Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD) 
is implementing a number of welfare schemes for rural areas of the country including 
Rajasthan viz., Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (Mahatma 
Gandhi NREGS), Pra dhan Mantri Awaas Yojana – Gramin (PMAY -G), Pradhan Mantri 
Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY), Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods 
Mission (DAY-NRLM), Deen Dayal Upadhayay – Gramin Kaushalya Yojana (DDU -GKY), 
Rural Self Employment Training Insti tutes (RSETIs), National Social Assistance Programme 
(NSAP) and Shyama Prasad   Mukherji Rurban Mission (SPMRM) to alleviate poverty in 
rural areas and to bring about overall improvement in the quality of life of the people in rural 
areas, strengthening of livelihood opportunities, providing minimum guaranteed employment, 
promoting self -employment, skilling of rural youths in various useful trades and 
entrepreneurship qualities, infrastructure development and provision of social assistance. 
Further, Departme nt of Land Resources (DoLR), MoRD is implementing Watershed 
Development Component (WDC) of Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) 
which is principally for development of rainfed portions of net cultivated area and culturable 
wastelands.   
  
All the  schemes are implemented through State Governments and no funds are being 
provided by the Union Government to Non -Governmental Organizations (NGOs) for 
implementing projects under rural development schemes in the country including Rajasthan. 
However, under  SPMRM, implementation at the State level is done by the State Nodal 
Agency under Rural Development/Panchayati Raj Department. Individual works selected for 
clusters are implemented by the agency identified in the Detailed Project Reports for the 
cluster, which includes concerned line department/ gram panchayat/ block/ executing agency 
etc. The implementation agencies may include non -governmental agencies during the 
implementation. However, the details of such association are not maintained by the Ministry.

EMPLOYMENT OF PEOPLE FROM 70 MILLION FAMILIES UNDER MGNREGS 
 
839.  SHRI RITESH PANDEY: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government is aware that the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural 
Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) is projected to employ people from 
over 70 million families in the financial Year 2022-23 on indication that overall 
economic growth is still not reaching the rural and unorganised sections of the 
country and if so, the details thereof; 
(b)  whether the Government is aware that as compared to the corresponding pre-COVID 
month of October 2019, about 15.5 million households applied for jobs through the 
MGNREGS in October 2022; 
(c)  if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; 
(d)  whether the Government is aware that in contrast to its two lakh target, the Unnati 
initiative, which was launched in 2020 to reduce reliance on the MGNREGS, has 
trained only 25,056 people; and 
(e)  if so, the reasons therefor along with the steps taken by the Government to address the 
issue? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a)to(c):  Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (Mahatma 
Gandhi NREGS) is a demand driven wage employment Scheme which provides for the 
enhancement of livelihood security of the households in rural areas of the country by 
providing at least one hundred days of guaranteed wage employment in every financial 
year to every household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work.   It 
provides livelihood security, i.e. fall back options for livelihood for t he rural households, 
when no better employment opportunity is available. 
  
In current financial year 2022 -23 (as on 03.02.2023), a total number of 5.78 crore 
household availed employment under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS. 
  
In the month of October, 2019, a total number of  1.29 crore households demanded 
employment under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS, whereas in the month of October, 2022, a 
total number of  1.55 crore households demanded employment under the Scheme. 
  
(d)&(e):  Yes, Sir. The Government is aware about the progress of Project Unnati. The 
Ministry is regularly reviewing the progress with the State Rural Livelihood Mission. All the 
issues that come to the Ministry are addressed immediately.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
DEPARTMENT OF ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 841 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 7TH FEBRUARY, 2023 
 
PROTECT1`ION OF STRAY CATTLE 
841.  SHRIMATI GOMATI SAI 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालनऔर डेयरी मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is contemplating to work out any new plan for protection of a stray 
cattle (cow progeny) in Jaspur and Raigarh Lok Sabha Constituency of Chhattisgarh; 
(b) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and 
(c) the number of new gaushalas opened/likely to be opened in coming years in the country 
including Raigarh and Jaspur area of Chhattisgarh? 
ANSWER 
        THE MINISTER FOR FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA) 
 
(a) & (b) The protection of animals is a state subject. As per information received from 
Government of Chhattishgarh, the Chhattisgarh Government is already executing scheme namely 
"Narwa, Garuwa, Ghuruwa and Badi" under which Gothans are established at Grarm Panchayat 
level where provision for protection of Cattle including Stray Cattle (cow progeny) is made. Apart 
from Gothan, State is also operating registered Goushalas where Stray Cattles can be kept. As has 
been reported by the State there are 1190 gothans  established in Jaspur and Raigarh  Lok Sabha 
constituency where Stray c attle are protected. In these Gothan s, the provision of dry and green 
fodder (as p er availability), drinking water, shed,veterinary aids etc. is made available. So, no 
further new plan is required for the protection of Stray Cattle in the state.  The Government is not 
contemplating to work out any new plan for protection of Stray Cattle (cow progeny) in Jashpur & 
Raigarh Lok Sabha constituency of Chhattisgarh as this is a state and local subject. 
 
(c)     In the above said constituency, there is 09 Goushalas registered under Chhattisgarh Rajay 
Goseva Ayog. The subsidy for feed and fodder, shed and medicines is released to Goushalas as per 
their demand. These Goushalas are run by NGO's for which subsidy is provided by the State 
Government. New Goushalas can be opend in this constituency as and when application received 
by the Chhattisgarh Rajay Goseva Ayog. Till date no applications have been received / pending for 
approval by the Chhattisgarh Rajay Goseva Ayog in this financial year as reported by the state 
government.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 842  
ANSWERED ON 07TH FEBRUARY, 2023 
 
FOREIGN INVESTMENT IN FOOD PROCESSING UNITS 
  
842.  SHRI KHAEGN MURMU: 
SHRI KANAKMAL KATARA:  
 
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be please to state: 
(a)  whether the Government has approved the proposals of foreign investments for setting up food 
processing units in the State of Rajasthan and West Bengal; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; and   
(c)  the effects/impact of the said foreign investments on the domestic small scale food processing 
industries?  
  
ANSWER 
 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES   
(SHRI PRAHLAD SINGH PATEL) 
  
(a) & (b) 100% Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) is permit ted through automatic route for 
manufacturing food products, except from the bordering countries. One FDI proposal of Rs 7,52,000/- 
in respect of M/s Himadriyati Food Products Pvt. Ltd at Darjeeling, West Bengal, has been approved. 
However, no proposal pertaining to Rajasthan has been received for Government approval.  
 
(c)      There is no evidence of any adverse impact of foreign investments on domestic small scale food 
processing industries. Foreign investments have assisted Small and Medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) 
in food processing sector with improved efficiency by breaking supply bottlenecks; introduction of 
innovative/new technologies; upgradation of skills for workforce; reduction in losses with modern 
techniques and quality control systems and pro cess standardisation, further boosting the capacity of 
the SMEs to manufacture export quality processed foods as per domestic and international standards.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 845 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 7TH FEBRUARY, 2023 
 
 Employment in Fisheries Sector 
 
 
845. SHRI SANJAY SETH: 
 
 
         Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING मत्स्यपालन, 
पशुपालन और डे यरी मंत्री be pleased to state:  
 
(a)  whether fisheries has emerged as a big employment creation sector and if so, the details thereof;  
 
(b) whether the Government is running any scheme to boost this sector and if so, the details thereof;    
 
(c) whether the Government has allocated funds to the States for fisheries and if so, the details thereof, 
State-wise; 
 
(d) the status of fish production in Jharkhand; 
 
(e) the quantum of fish produced by the groups engaged in fisheries during the last two years; and 
 
(f) the number of people who got self-employment in this sector?   
 
 
ANSWER 
 
 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING: 
 
(SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA) 
(a) to (c):   The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, An imal Husbandry and Dairying through the 
scheme of Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) inter-alia envisages to generate direct and 
indirect employment opportunities to about 55 lakh personnel in fisheries and aquaculture sector by 2024 -25. 
The PMMS Y at an estimated investment of Rs. 20,050 crore with array of more than 100  components/sub-
components is implemented in all the States and Union Territories including Government of Jharkhand for a 
period of 5 years from financial year 2020 -21 to 2024 -25.  The scheme aims to create direct and indirect 
employment opportunities for fishers, fish farmers, fish workers, fish vendors, entrepreneurs and enhance 
income of fishers and other stakeholders  etc., through the implementation of various targeted intervent ions in 
fish production, productivity, fisheries infrastructure and marketing. 
 
The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying during last two 
financial years (2020 -21 and 2021 -22) and current year (2022 -23) has accorded approvals to the proposals of 
various States/UTs and other implementing agencies amounting Rs. 11783.17 crore with central share of Rs. 
4405.06 crore under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY). The state -wise details of the 
projects approved, c entral funds sanctioned and released during last two years of implementation of PMMSY 
i.e. 2020-21, 2021-22 and 2022-23 (as on date) are furnished at Annexure-I 
(d) and (e): The fish production of Jharkhand has been recorded at 2.57 lakh ton nes during the year 2021-22. 
The country’s fish production during 2020 -21 and 2021 -22 stands at 147.25 lakh tons and  162.48 lakh tons 
respectively. 
(f):   It is estimated that the activities taken up so far under the PMMSY , has the potential to create 8.55 lakh 
direct employment opportunities and 25.66 lakh indirect employment opportunities in fisheries and aquaculture.

TO BE ANSWERED ON 7TH FEBRUARY 2023 
 
CONSERVATION OF INDIGENOUS COW SPECIES 
 
846. SHRI OMPRAKASH BHUPALSINH ALIAS PAWAN RAJENIMBALKAR: 
SHRI VINAYAK RAUT: 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालनऔरडेयरीमंत्री 
be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that Brazil has developed milching capacity of Gir cow breed from 
thirty litre to forty litre every day;  
(b) if so, whether the Government is contemplating any proposal in reference to Gir, Kakrapar and Khillar 
breeds in the country;  
(c) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor;  
(d) the details of the provisions made by the Government for conservation of indigenous cow breeds like 
Gir, Kakrapar and Khillar found in Maharashtra and Karnataka;  
(e) the details of the number  of gaushalas in Maharashtra provided financial assistance by the 
Government for conservation of cows; and  
(f) the details of proposals to begin schemes to boost milk production and to start projects of companies 
producting like Amul Milk in the State of Maharashtra? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER FOR FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
 (SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA) 
 
(a) to (d) Yes, Sir. Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying is implementing Rashtriya  
Gokul Mission for development and conservation of indigenous bovine breeds and genetic upgradation of 
bovine population since December 2014. The scheme is important for increasing the production and 
productivity of milk thereby making dairying more remunerative for farmers of the country. The scheme 
is continued u nder revised and realigned schemes of the Department from 2021 -22 to 2025 -26 with an 
allocation of Rs.2400 crore. All indigenous breeds of cattle including Gir, Tharparkar, and Khillar  are 
covered under the scheme. 
 
(e) For development and conservation of indigenous breeds of cattle , funds are released to 
Maharashtra Livestock Development Board  under the scheme Rashtriya Gokul Mission . Central 
Government do not release funds directly to stakeholders. All stake holders including gaushalas having a 
role in cattle and buffalo development are integrated for implementation of the project by State Livestock 
Development Board.The details of Gaushalas in Maharashtra assisted by Animal Welfare Board of India  
during the last 5 years is at Annexure-I 
 
(f) In order to  boost milk production and to strengthen dairy sector in the country including in the 
State of Maharashtra the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying is implementing the following 
schemes: (i) Rashtriya  Gokul Mission; (ii) National Programme for Dairy  Development; (iii) Dairy 
Processing and Infrastructure Development Fund; (iv) Support ing Dairy Cooperatives  and Farmers 
Producers Organisations; and (vi) Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS 
(DEPARTMENT OF SPORTS) 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No.847 
ANSWERED ON 07/02/2023 
 
Participation of India in International Sports for Persons with 
Disabilities  
 
847. MS. DIYA KUMARI:  
 
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the steps currently being taken by the Government to increase 
international participation of India in sports for persons with 
disabilities;  
 
(b) whether the Government has taken any m easures to promote the 
participation of persons with disabilities in sports competitions at the 
international level including the Paralympic Games;  
 
(c) if so, the details thereof;  
 
(d) whether the Government is considering the need to build new, 
disabled-friendly sports stadiums or complexes to increase the 
participation of youth with disabilities in sports and if so, the details 
thereof; and  
 
(e) whether the Government has undertaken any measures to ensure 
equal recruitment opportunities for sportspers ons with disabilities 
across the country, State/UT-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS 
(SHRI ANURAG SINGH THAKUR) 
 
(a) to (c) Government provides finan cial assistance to the National  
Sports Federations (NSFs) viz., the Paralympic Committee of India 

(PCI),  the All IndiaSports Council for Deaf (AISCD), the Special 
Olympic Bharat (SOB) and  the Cerebral Palsy Sports Federation of 
India (CPSFI) towards training of sports personal with disabilities  for 
their participation in international events including Paralympic Games. 
The athletes selected for international competitions are provided with 
all requisite facilities for their preparations including  wholesome 
nutritious diet, food supplements, equipment support, state -of-the-art 
infrastructure, lodging, travelling facilities, services  of reputed Indian 
and Foreign Coaches/  supporting staff, scientific & medical 
support,sports kit, etc. Under Target Olympic PodiumScheme (TOPS), 
talented athletes are selected and provided financialassistance like 
Out of Pocket Allowance, equipment  support, coaches etc ., for their 
customized training. Athletes are retained in the TOPS based on the 
regular assessment of their performance.  
 
(d) Yes,  Sir. T o promote sports among the persons with disa bilities, 
SAI has established a Para  Centre under SAI’s National Centre of 
Excellence (NCOE) Scheme at  SAI Regional Centre, Gandhinagar. The 
center is operational in the disciplines of Athletics, Swimming, 
Powerlifting & Table Tennis. All  the SAI Stadiums and training centres 
have been made disabled -friendly and up -gradation of th e same is 
carried out from time -to-time to ensure comfort of sports person with 
disabilities. Under the component “Promotion of Inclusiveness through 
Sports” of the Khelo India Scheme, sports infrastructure and training 
centers are created so as to ensure effective participation of Persons 
with Disabilities. 
 
(e) Yes. Recruitment of meritorious sportspersons , including 
persons with disabilities  is done as per Government Guidelines. More 
chances are given to the recruitment opportunities of personswith 
disabilities in almost all States.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 848 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 07TH FEBRUARY, 2023/ MAGHA 18, 1944 (SAKA) 
 
LOSSES CAUSED DUE TO NATURAL DISASTER 
 
848.    SHRIMATI CHINTA ANURADHA: 
           SHRI MADDILA GURUMOORTHY: 
           SHRI M.V.V. SATYANARAYANA: 
           SHRI KURUVA GORANTLA MADHAV: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the  devastating combination of heavy 
rains, floods and the cyclone which affected Andhra Pradesh in 2021  and if so, 
the details thereof; 
 
(b) whether any central assistance was provided  to the State as interim relief 
to tide over this time; 
 
(c) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; 
 
(d) whether the  Inter-Ministerial Central Team  (IMCT) was sent to assess the 
damage and losses caused by heavy rains in Andhra Pradesh; and 
 
(e) if so, the details thereof including the date of  assessment after the disaster 
took place and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
(a) to (e): As per the National Policy on Disaster Management, the primary 
responsibility for disaster management, including disbursal of relief to the 
affected people on the ground level, rests with the State Governments 
concerned.  The State Governments undertake re lief measures in the wake of 
natural disasters from the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF), already 
placed   at   their   disposal,   in   accordance  with  the  Government  of  India’s  
 

 -2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 848  FOR 07.02.2023 
approved  items  and  norms.   Additional  financial  assistance  is provided 
from   the   National   Disaster  Response  Fund  (NDRF),  as  per  laid  down 
procedure in case of disaster of ‘severe nature’, which includes an assessment 
based on the visit of an Inter-Ministerial Central Team (IMCT). 
The State Government of Andhra Pradesh vide their letter dated 
22.11.2021 had informed about the damages caused by heavy rains to crops, 
roads, transmission lines etc. to the tune of Rs. 6054.29 crore and requested 
for the immediate release  of Rs. 1000 crore for restoration and relief 
operations. 
 The Central Government, without waiting for the Memorandum from the 
State Government of Andhra Pradesh, constituted an IMCT on 23 rd November, 
2021, for on the spot assessment of damages.  IMCT visited the State on 26 -29 
November, 2021.  Based on the report of IMCT and recommendations of Sub -
Committee of the National Executive Committee (SC -NEC), the High Level 
Committee (HLC) had appr oved an amount of Rs. 351.43 crore to the State 
Government of Andhra Pradesh, which has  since been released to the State 
Government. 
Besides, during the financial year 2021 -22, the State Government was 
allocated Rs. 1192.80 crore under SDRF, which included  Rs. 895.20 crore as 
Central share and Rs. 297.60 crore as State share.  The Central share of  Rs. 
895.20 crore was released, in advance, to the Government of Andhra Pradesh in 
two installments of Rs. 447.60 crore each.

Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has empowered the   district collectors of two 
more districts in Gujarat – Mehsana, and Anand – to grant citizenship 
certificates to the members of Hindu, Sikh, Parsi, Christian, Buddhist and 
Jain communities from Pakistan, Afghanistan and Bangladesh; 
 
(b) if so, the criteria used by the Government to  grant citizenship to people 
specifically from the religions mentioned above; and  
 
(c) the reasons for choosing specifica lly the districts as mentioned above 
in Gujarat to grant citizenship certificates? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
(a) to (c): Yes Sir.  The Central Government, in exercise of powers 
conferred by Section 16 of The Citizenship Act, 1955, has delegated its 
power to grant citizenship by registration under Section 5 and by 
naturalisation under Section 6 of The Citizenship Act, 1955 to the 
Collectors of 31 Districts including Mehsana and Anand, Gujarat for speedy 
disposal   of   citizenship   applications   of   person   belonging  to  minority

communities of Pakistan, Afghanistan and Bangladesh namely, Hindu, Sikh, 
Jain,  Buddhist,  Parsi  and  Christian.  This delegation of power is aimed at  
speedy disposal of the citizenship applications of such foreigners as

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING  
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 852 
(TO BE ANSWERED ON 07.02.2023) 
 
Frequency of Community Radio.  
 
852. SHRI T.N. PRATHAPAN: 
 
Will the Minister of INFORMATION & BROADCASTING be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of current frequency range of a Community Radio Station (CRS) and 
also the details of average accessibility of frequency range of CRS in the 
country;  
(b) whether the Government will increase the frequency range as double of the 
current range; 
(c) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor;  
(d) whether the Government can allow a special frequency range considering the 
focused communities like education, agriculture etc. and if so, the details 
thereof;  
(e) whether the Government will increase the time advertisements during the 
programme transmission and if so, the details thereof; and  
(f) whether the Government proposes to amend the copyright laws to allow free of 
cost accessibility of film songs for CRS and if so, the details thereof? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
 
THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING; AND 
MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS  
(SHRI ANURAG SINGH THAKUR) 
 
(a) As per provisions of the ‘Policy Guidelines for setting up Community Radio 
Stations (CRS) in India’ , CRS is expected to cover a range of 5 -10 km. For 
this, a transmitter having maximum Effective Radiated Power (ERP) of 100 
W is adequate. However, the actual range of a Community Radio Station 
may differ from place to place and depends on topography of the terrain. 

(b)  (c) & (d) The Policy Guidelines provide that, in case of a proven need where 
the applicant organization is able to establish that it needs to serve a larger 
area or the terrain so warrants, higher transmitter wattage with maximum 
ERP up to 250 Watts can b e considered on a case -to-case basis, subject to 
availability of frequency and such other clearances as necessary from the 
Ministry of Communication. Requests for higher transmitter power above 
100 Watts and upto 250 Watts is subject to approval by the Int er-Ministerial 
Committee. 
 
(e) As per the policy guidelines, limited advertising and announcements relating 
to local events, local businesses and services and employment opportunities 
are allowed on Community Radio Stations. The maximum duration of such 
limited advertising is restricted to 7 (seven) minutes per hour of broadcast. 
 
(f) The Ministry has not proposed any amendment in the copyright laws to allow 
free of cost accessibility of film songs for CRS.
